meta.scope: Indonesia Batch 17 (final polish) — Subnational fiscal (district/city government finance, DAU/DAK equalisation) and water resources / water-supply statistics. Closes the two remaining high-value gaps before moving to the next country.

candidates.title: District/City Government Finance Statistics (Statistik Keuangan Pemerintah Kabupaten/Kota)
candidates.description: Annual statistics on the revenues and expenditures of district and city governments across Indonesia. Captures the fiscal capacity and spending patterns of the lowest significant tier of subnational government.
candidates.notes: Core subnational fiscal node at kabupaten/kota level.

candidates.title: Fiscal equalisation transfers (DAU, DAK, DBH)
candidates.description: The main intergovernmental transfer instruments: Dana Alokasi Umum (general equalisation), Dana Alokasi Khusus (special purpose, including disaster), and Dana Bagi Hasil (revenue sharing). Central to understanding how resources are redistributed across a highly unequal archipelago.
candidates.notes: Equalisation-mechanism node. Critical for spatial fiscal equity.

candidates.title: Subnational own-source revenue (PAD) statistics and capacity
candidates.description: Statistics and analysis of Pendapatan Asli Daerah (own-source revenue). Most districts remain heavily transfer-dependent; PAD capacity varies sharply and interacts with the DAU formula.
referenced_by: Local government finance and DAU/DAK nodes
candidates.notes: Own-source counterpart to the transfer system.

candidates.title: Water Supply Statistics
candidates.description: Annual statistics from the Water Supply Company Survey covering clean-water production, distribution and related indicators. Provides the formal water-utility statistical base.

candidates.title: Water resources and irrigation / agricultural water indicators
candidates.publisher: BPS Agricultural Indicators / Ministry of Public Works & Housing related
candidates.description: Statistical and indicator material on water resources relevant to agriculture and broader use, including irrigation-related series. Java’s high population and agricultural intensity make water stress a recurring spatial and policy theme.
candidates.notes: Resource-side water node that links food security, environment and spatial concentration.

candidates.title: Java water-stress and water-security framing
candidates.publisher: Derived from water-supply, agricultural and planning sources
candidates.description: Recurring policy and analytical framing of water stress on Java — high population density, intensive agriculture, industrial demand and seasonal variability. Complements the national water-supply statistics with a spatially focused narrative.
referenced_by: Water Supply Statistics and irrigation indicators
candidates.notes: Spatial water-stress node that tightens the Java environmental and infrastructure cluster.

candidates.title: Indonesia subnational-fiscal and water densification meta-node
candidates.publisher: Derived from BPS local-finance and water-supply sources
candidates.description: Meta-node binding district/city government finance statistics, DAU/DAK/DBH equalisation transfers, own-source revenue (PAD), Water Supply Statistics, irrigation/water-resource indicators, and Java water-stress framing into the final polish layer.
referenced_by: All detailed nodes in this batch
Earlier APBN, government-accounts, environmental and Java series
candidates.notes: Closing integrating node for the final polish round.
